Structured pruning further indicates that the model can retain spatial structure under substantial compression, while spectral fidelity becomes notably more sensitive beyond roughly 70% pruning.

title: BCP3D: Robust 3D Object Tracking Using Brain-Inspired Complementary-Pathway for Challenging Scenarios
Synergizing Disentangled Representation and Split Federated Learning to Break Centralized Bottlenecks in Gaze Estimation
Cross3DReg: A Real-world Cross-source Point Cloud Registration Benchmark
Global offshore wind development (2015–2025): multiscale structural evolution based on object-level sar mapping
abstract: Offshore wind is an important renewable infrastructure supporting the global energy transition, making accurate offshore wind turbine (OWT) mapping essential for understanding infrastructure expansion and informing marine spatial management. Existing long-term approaches often extend single-period detections over time based on structural-stability assumptions, but accumulated identification errors and regional imaging differences limit consistent object-level representation across years and regions. To address this challenge, this study proposes a coordinated three-stage object-level SAR mapping framework, in which a stable and balanced sample representation strategy under unified annual temporal windows provides a consistent data basis across regions and years. On this basis, the lightweight YOLO-SAR model integrates frequency-aware feature modeling and hierarchical structural representation to improve OWT detection under heterogeneous conditions. Compared with YOLO11n, YOLO-SAR reduces the parameter count from 2.58 M to 2.30 M while improving mAP@0.5:0.95 from 0.3956 to 0.4553. Spatial reconstruction then transforms detection outputs into consistent annual object-level OWT maps, forming a continuous spatial database covering 2015–2025. Multi-region validation and comparisons with public datasets further support the reliability of these spatial records. These records reveal multiscale patterns of offshore wind spatial evolution: shifts in regional contributions reshape global growth, regional expansion pathways and internal spatial restructuring exhibit stage-dependent differences, and site-boundary expansion and turbine-spacing adjustments determine local spatial organization. These findings demonstrate that global offshore wind development is not merely a process of quantitative growth, but a multiscale spatial evolution driven by regional shifts, site expansion, and internal spatial reorganization. The proposed framework provides a consistent data foundation for global offshore wind evolution analysis and can be extended to other marine energy infrastructures.

title: LexSign: Learning Sign Language from Lexical Descriptions
Zero-Shot Domain Generalization via Domain Prompt Learning
An interpretable DM-PINN for retrieving mangrove canopy carbon, nitrogen, and potassium contents using Sentinel-2 and SDGSAT-1 observations along China's southeastern coast
abstract: Mangroves are among the most important blue carbon ecosystems, contributing substantially to global carbon sequestration and biodiversity conservation. Canopy carbon (CCC), nitrogen (CNC), and potassium (CKC) contents provide critical indicators of nutrient cycling, ecosystem functioning, and ecological health. However, the structural complexity and strong spatial heterogeneity of mangroves present major obstacles to understanding the spectral response mechanisms and achieving reliable large-scale retrieval of these biochemical parameters. To address these limitations, we developed an interpretable retrieval framework that integrates causal analysis with physical constraints for reliable estimation of mangrove biochemical parameters. First, we proposed a Multi-Channel Chatterjee-Enhanced Correlation Spectrum Analysis (MC-ξ-CS) method that integrates causal discovery to systematically identify spectral bands causally associated with CCC, CNC, and CKC. For large-scale retrieval of mangrove canopy parameters, the identified causal relationships were transferred to satellite observations through a Global Angle-Divergence Spectral Transfer (GADT) framework, yielding robust estimation (R2 = 0.511–0.669). Subsequently, a Dual-Mechanism Guided Physics-Informed Neural Network (DM-PINN) was developed to synergistically integrate causal analysis and physical constraints, achieving robust retrieval performance (R2 = 0.604–0.83) for three representative mangrove species and enhancing the physical interpretability of the results. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first comprehensive large-scale retrieval of key mangrove biochemical parameters along the southeastern coast of China, revealing CCC values of 409.18–566.89 g/kg (C/N = 9.77–14.21), CNC values of 14.38–74.9 g/kg (N/K = 1.99–3.86), and CKC values of 4.78–19.67 g/kg (C/K = 28.22–37.67). Distinct inter-provincial spatial patterns were observed: CNC and CKC exhibited similar gradients, increasing from landward to seaward regions, whereas CCC displayed an opposite spatial distribution pattern with lower values in coastal regions. Moreover, CCC was strongly positively correlated with CNC, while CKC showed negative correlations with both parameters. Collectively, this study established a novel theoretical and methodological framework for elucidating the spectral response mechanisms of mangrove biochemical parameters, offering critical scientific support for large-scale mangrove degradation monitoring, ecological restoration assessment, and biodiversity conservation.

title: Wavelet-guided decomposition of two-dimensional InSAR time series: insights into long-term settlement and cyclic deformation of a high earth-rockfill dam
abstract: Long-term deformation of high earth-rockfill dams reflects post-construction consolidation, creep, reservoir loading, and cyclic operation. Separating these superimposed components is essential for gaining process-level insights into spatial patterns and differential responses. This study investigates the Pubugou Dam, a 186 m high earth-rockfill dam in Southwest China, using ascending and descending Sentinel-1 observations from 2017–2023. The two viewing geometries were jointly inverted to recover vertical and east-west displacements. A wavelet-guided decomposition, in which dominant periods identified by the continuous wavelet transform constrain the window length and component grouping in singular spectrum analysis, was proposed to separate the displacement records into long-term trend, annual cyclic, and residual components. Synthetic experiments yielded root mean square errors of 0.69–2.16 mm, indicating effective decomposition performance. Cross wavelet transform and wavelet transform coherence quantified localized coherence and phase lags between the cyclic components and reservoir water level. The central earth-rockfill body exhibits the largest magnitudes of vertical and east-west deformation rates, whereas the spillway and abutments remained comparatively stable. The trend components and settlement indices are consistent with relatively slow long-term post-construction settlement during the observation period. Annual cyclic deformation is more pronounced in the east-west direction and exhibits spatially variable lags relative to reservoir level fluctuations. Settlement inclination and apparent horizontal strain remain low under the adopted criteria, suggesting limited crest-cracking susceptibility during the observation period. This work demonstrates how wavelet-guided decomposition of two-dimensional InSAR time series provides spatially explicit insights into long-term settlement and cyclic deformation of high earth-rockfill dams.

title: Reconstructing multi-temporal Glacier area changes to improve mass balance estimates in the Southeastern Tibetan Plateau (2000–2025)
abstract: The southeastern Tibetan Plateau (SETP), a critical component of the “Asian Water Tower”, hosts a large concentration of maritime temperate glaciers that are highly sensitive to climate change. However, persistent cloud cover, seasonal snow, and supraglacial debris complicate consistent long-term glacier mapping, while the use of static glacier boundaries may introduce temporal mismatches in altimetry-based glacier mass-change estimates. In this study, we developed a multi-source data-fusion framework on Google Earth Engine (GEE) to reconstruct glacier-area changes in the SETP from 2000 to 2025 at five-year intervals and 30 m spatial resolution. Random Forest classifiers were used to integrate Landsat and Sentinel-2 optical imagery, Sentinel-1 synthetic-aperture-radar data, and NASADEM-derived topographic information, supporting glacier delineation under complex surface and atmospheric conditions. The reconstructed glacier area decreased from 8,083 ± 664 km2 in 2000 to 6,228 ± 572 km2 in 2025, corresponding to a cumulative loss of 22.9 ± 3.6% and a mean loss rate of 80.51 ± 10.51 km2 yr−1. The mean area-loss rates were 51.31 ± 6.51 km2 yr−1 during 2000–2010 and 92.99 ± 15.55 km2 yr−1 during 2010–2025, indicating a higher average loss rate in the later period. By combining satellite-altimetry-derived elevation changes from ICESat, CryoSat-2, and ICESat-2 with the reconstructed time-varying glacier areas, we estimated a mean glacier mass-change rate of −6.51 ± 1.22 Gt yr−1 during 2003–2022. Compared with using a fixed 2003 glacier area, the time-varying-area calculation reduced the estimated mass-loss magnitude by 0.63 Gt yr−1, equivalent to 8.8% of the fixed-area estimate. These results indicate that incorporating time-varying glacier areas can reduce temporal mismatch in altimetry-based mass-change estimation and improve the temporal consistency of regional glacier mass-change assessments.

title: Second-dimension-enhanced spatial context-aware modeling for spatial prediction
abstract: Spatial prediction is a fundamental task in geographic information science and environmental resource assessment. However, under complex terrain and heterogeneous covariates, models relying only on point-scale attributes or a single global relationship often have difficulty representing spatial context and regional heterogeneity. This study proposes a second-dimension-enhanced spatial context-aware modeling framework (SDA-SCA) that integrates first-dimension covariates, neighborhood-based second-dimension features, covariate screening, spatially constrained stratification, and local model training. Using two independently constructed annual spatial-prediction cases based on surface solar radiation observations from 670 stations in China in 2022 and 2023, five modeling schemes—Ordinary Kriging, Geographically Weighted Random Forest (GWRF), first-dimension attribute modeling (FDA), second-dimension augmented modeling (SDA), and SDA-SCA—were evaluated under spatial cross-validation. SDA-SCA showed a consistent predictive advantage across the two independent annual cases and the three evaluated model families. Relative to FDA, SDA-SCA increased R2 by 0.11–0.16 in 2022 and 0.17–0.21 in 2023, while reducing RMSE by 12.4%–17.7% and 24.3%–33.7%, and MAE by 22.8%–35.5% and 31.5%–50.4%, respectively. Stage-wise ablation showed that the FDA-to-SDA step produced consistent but moderate improvements, whereas the SDA-to-SDA-SCA step provided larger and more stable gains. These results indicate that second-dimension features improve the representation of neighborhood context, and their predictive value is further strengthened when coupled with spatial stratification. SHAP analysis further confirmed the substantial contribution of second-dimension features to the integrated model. The proposed framework provides an extensible pathway for spatial prediction tasks requiring the joint representation of local attributes, neighborhood context, and spatial heterogeneity.

title: Transforming Leaf-Off LiDAR to leaf-on canopy height models using deep learning
abstract: Accurate tree canopy metrics are essential for a wide range of ecological, environmental, and climate studies. Recent advances in airborne LiDAR sensing have greatly expanded access to high-resolution three-dimensional observations of tree canopy structure. However, many widely available airborne LiDAR datasets are acquired under leaf-off conditions to support terrain mapping, and our analysis across ecologically diverse sites shows that canopy height models (CHMs) derived from these data exhibit substantial, recurring discrepancies in canopy height and extent, with an overall tendency to underrepresent canopy structure relative to leaf-on conditions. These discrepancies limit the direct use of leaf-off CHMs in applications requiring canopy information representative of leaf-on conditions. To address this limitation, we introduce a deep learning framework for reconstructing leaf-on CHMs from existing leaf-off LiDAR-derived CHMs. To our knowledge, this is the first study to formulate the direct reconstruction of leaf-on CHMs from existing leaf-off LiDAR-derived CHMs as a supervised image-to-image learning task. The framework provides two complementary models: a Pix2Pix model that uses the leaf-off CHM alone and a U-Net model that additionally incorporates multispectral imagery. Our proposed models achieve robust canopy-height accuracy across four spatially independent test sites (R²: 0.85–0.92; Mean Absolute Error: 1.3–1.6 metres), substantially reducing the discrepancies observed in the leaf-off source CHMs. They also provide sharper delineation of canopy details and higher accuracy than recent optical-imagery-based approaches. To facilitate broader use, we developed an open-access web application that deploys the pre-trained models and supports on-demand leaf-on CHM generation for user-selected areas across the U.S. where suitable leaf-off LiDAR inputs are available. Overall, the framework provides a practical means to bridge the seasonal data gap in LiDAR acquisition and improve access to reliable canopy metrics representative of leaf-on conditions.

title: Deep learning detection of submesoscale eddies from MODIS SST in the South China Sea
abstract: Submesoscale eddies play crucial roles in oceanic energy cascades and material transport; however, their detection faces substantial challenges owing to inadequate spatial resolution in traditional satellite altimetric measurements. This research introduces Sub-Eddy-Net, an innovative deep learning approach utilizing an enhanced YOLOv8-SGAM architecture for identifying submesoscale eddy features within MODIS-derived sea surface temperature (SST) imagery across the South China Sea region. By exploiting SST data's advantageous temporal coverage and observational continuity relative to altimetric sensors, synthetic aperture radar, and ocean color products, the developed algorithm demonstrates detection precision of 0.968, successfully identifying 20,443 submesoscale eddies throughout 2015–2024. Results indicate cyclonic eddy prevalence exceeds anticyclonic occurrences, exhibiting average radii of 13.1 km and 13.7 km respectively. Eddy distributions primarily cluster within coastal waters and Luzon Strait vicinity, displaying pronounced seasonal patterns. Comparison with Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) observations shows 64.3% matched features, 27.1% positional offsets, and 8.6% detected only in SST. Within the same eddies, coherent chlorophyll-a (Chla) signatures were present in a smaller fraction, indicating that SST is the more robust tracer for systematic detection. This Sub-Eddy-Net methodology offers a scalable approach for examining submesoscale oceanic phenomena, providing a decadal inventory for further study of their roles in ocean circulation and vertical exchange.

title: A GeoAI framework for remote-sensing-driven traffic activity and emission intensity in a data-scarce megacity
abstract: In rapidly expanding megacities across the Global South, a profound data scarcity paradox frequently prevents effective environmental monitoring and evidence driven urban planning. While severe traffic congestion generates acute localised pollution, the total absence of continuous municipal traffic counters, ubiquitous vehicle telemetry, and air quality monitoring networks leaves these environments empirically unmonitored. This study resolves this challenge by introducing a reproducible geocomputational framework designed to map microscale traffic activity and relative emission landscapes by fusing multisource geospatial data and deep learning workflows. Focusing on the unmonitored context of Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, our methodology uses very high resolution 15 cm satellite imagery to train and deploy a localised YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once, version 8) computer vision model, establishing an empirical baseline of fleet distribution. These static counts are dynamically distributed across the urban road network using a probabilistic Hub and Spoke Gravity Model, which is weighted through a zero shot Large Language Model semantic reclassification of unstructured OpenStreetMap features. Reconstructed kinematic flows are subsequently processed through velocity dependent Tier 3 EMEP/EEA algorithms to capture the nonlinear emission penalties triggered by severe network gridlock. To ensure framework defensibility, an independent unmanned aerial vehicle observation campaign was executed across ten distinct urban sites. The drone data directly validate model estimated physical parameters, achieving robust correlations for traffic volumes (R2 = 0.826) and link speeds (R2 = 0.925). Because literature derived chemical emission factors cannot be validated in situ, all absolute outputs are subjected to a rigorous multiparameter sensitivity analysis to report findings strictly as bounded ranges. The results reveal a clear structural handover in the spatial activity profile of the city. Daytime pollution is heavily driven by the informal paratransit fleet, which accounts for a bounded range of 82.8% to 95.1% of total PM2.5 emissions along primary corridors despite representing a numerical minority of active vehicles. Conversely, nocturnal baseline emissions transition to a landscape dominated almost entirely by private passenger vehicles. All code, processing pipelines, and validation datasets are available in a FAIR compliant open access repository. This framework establishes a scalable, remote sensing driven blueprint for diagnosing traffic activity structures in unmonitored metropolitan regions worldwide.

title: Integrating multi-source physical knowledge into deep learning for satellite soil moisture downscaling
abstract: Fine-resolution soil moisture (SM) is essential for understanding land–atmosphere interactions and managing hydrological hazards at local scales. Passive microwave remote sensing provides reliable SM observations but is limited by its coarse spatial resolution. Spatial downscaling offers an important means of addressing this limitation. However, many existing downscaling methods either rely on physical models with over-simplifications of soil hydrological knowledge, or data-driven models (particularly Deep Learning, DL) that lack interpretability, while current physics-guided DL approaches often emphasize a limited number of physical relationships or constraints. In response, this study proposes a framework to integrate multi-source physical knowledge into DL for satellite SM downscaling. Specifically, the framework incorporates physically informed drivers, a DisPATCh-informed physical regression branch, a hydrologically motivated consistency loss, and a constrained SM boundary loss, while using a gating module to adaptively fuse physically guided and data-driven representations. Evaluations based on in-situ and aircraft SM observations, together with coarse-scale consistency checks against SMAP SM, show that the proposed framework can effectively downscale SMAP SM from 9 km to 500 m. Using region-specific models across ten environmentally diverse regions, MPhy achieved station-averaged Pearson’s R and ubRMSE values of 0.76 and 0.05 m3/m3, respectively; the corresponding values for the pure-DL baseline Dens were 0.68 and 0.06 m3/m3. Detailed experiments in WGEW further showed that MPhy generally performed better than the pure-DL baseline, DisPATCh, single-physics-informed models, and selected conventional machine-learning methods. Overall, the results support improved physical plausibility and convergence efficiency, as well as framework robustness across the evaluated environments.

title: Adaptive smooth constrained stereo matching and disparity refinement for satellite DSM generation
abstract: High-resolution satellite images often exhibit substantial geometric and radiometric differences, making it difficult for conventional stereo matching methods to achieve high matching accuracy while suppressing noise and preserving object boundaries. To address this issue, this study improves both stereo matching and disparity post-processing in the satellite digital surface model (DSM) generation workflow. First, within the semi-global matching (SGM) framework, a mixed matching cost is constructed by combining the Census transform and gradient descriptors. Image gradients and edge cues extracted by a pretrained PiDiNet are then incorporated to adaptively control the strength of the smoothness constraint during cost aggregation, thereby improving matching reliability while balancing noise suppression and disparity-boundary preservation. Second, we propose a disparity post-processing method that combines improved weighted least-squares disparity refinement with matching-cost-based disparity fusion. The method first dynamically adjusts the smoothing weights to reduce texture-copying artifacts and edge blurring and then fuses disparity using matching costs to alleviate staircase artifacts caused by excessive smoothing. Experiments were conducted on ZY3-02 and WorldView-3 satellite imagery, with SGM, S2P-HD, Agisoft Metashape software, guided aggregation net, and FoundationStereo included for comparison. Across three test scenes dominated by urban and agricultural areas, the proposed method increased the proportion of pixels with absolute elevation errors below 2 m by an average of 4.12 percentage points and reduced RMSE by an average of 0.11 m compared with standard SGM. Qualitative results further show that the proposed method effectively suppresses noise in relatively flat regions while preserving building boundaries.

title: A large-scale spatiotemporal NDVI prediction method coupling multivariable constraints and structured modeling
abstract: Accurate prediction of vegetation dynamics is essential for understanding terrestrial ecosystems carbon and water cycles. However, existing Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) prediction methods are limited in their ability to represent spatiotemporal heterogeneity and nonlinear interactions among multiple driving variables, which restrict predictive accuracy and extrapolation performance at large scales. To address these limitations, this study proposed a structured large-scale NDVI spatiotemporal prediction method incorporating multivariable constraints (MCS-LSTP) to characterize vegetation dynamics in complex and heterogeneous environments. MCS-LSTP incorporates multiple key driving variables and enhances the comprehensive representation of complex spatiotemporal dependencies and spatial heterogeneity through homogeneous spatial unit partitioning, unit-level temporal modeling, and continuous surface reconstruction. Results showed that MCS-LSTP model exhibited superior performance in terms of stability and prediction accuracy when compared to AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Random Forest (RF), and Transformer models. The mean Population Stability Index (PSI) reached 0.0572, with 98.7% of prediction units exhibiting PSI values below 0.1, indicating no significant deviation between the observed and simulated NDVI values. The average R2 and RMSE on the test set were 0.8551 and 0.2171, respectively. Furthermore, MCS-LSTP accurately reproduced seasonal NDVI fluctuations and meridional spatial gradients, with particularly high agreement between simulated and reference values during the growing season. This study provides a robust and scalable solution for large-scale NDVI spatiotemporal prediction and offers critical technical support for ecological risk assessment in the Yellow River Basin and other ecologically vulnerable regions.

title: Hillslope-scale daily snow cover reconstruction in complex mountains: a novel framework integrating long-term snow persistence
abstract: Spatially continuous daily snow cover mapping at the hillslope scale (<100 m) is essential for resolving terrain-induced heterogeneity in hydrological processes and supporting mountain infrastructure management. Yet accurately characterizing daily snow cover heterogeneity at this scale remains challenging due to observational limitations and the difficulty of resolving terrain-controlled snow accumulation and ablation dynamics. To address this challenge, we developed a hillslope-scale daily snow cover reconstruction (HDSR) framework that explicitly incorporates long-term snow persistence as a structural spatial prior. The framework reconciles coarse-resolution daily Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI) observations with a 30 m climatological snow cover frequency (SCOF) dataset, which characterizes terrain-mediated long-term snow persistence and constrains the spatial allocation of daily snow cover at the sub-pixel scale. HDSR is implemented through three sequential stages: spatiotemporal continuity restoration (STR), SCOF-constrained spatial refinement (SSR), and spatiotemporal snow-cover inference (SSI). A high-quality 30 m reference dataset was first constructed using the Snow Mapping Algorithm Considering Different Lighting Conditions (SALC), which was identified as the optimal approach through a systematic evaluation of seven candidate snow-mapping methods. The HDSR framework was subsequently applied to the Qilian Mountains and adjacent regions (QMAR), generating a daily 30 m binary snow cover product over an extensive mountainous region (536,018 km2) from September 2013 to August 2025. Validation against independent Landsat 8 observations yielded an F1-score (FS) of 0.873 and Cohen’s kappa (CK) of 0.859, while Bias values close to unity indicated negligible systematic bias in snow-cover representation. Consistent results obtained from independent Landsat 9 observations and time-lapse photography further supported the validity of the reconstruction, although site-specific evaluation revealed reduced capability for reconstructing short-lived snow events. The reconstructed dataset markedly outperforms the corresponding coarse-resolution baseline while providing enhanced spatial details. Compared with machine-learning models that exclude SCOF-related predictors, the proposed framework yields notable improvements, increasing FS and CK by 4.1% and 4.6%, respectively. Long-term snow persistence provides unique information unavailable from daily MODIS observations alone and is essential for resolving hillslope-scale snow heterogeneity. This study advances hillslope-scale daily snow cover mapping and potentially contributes to improved hydrological modeling and snow hazard assessment in complex mountainous environments.

title: SAMWater: a prompt-guided multimodal framework for transferable water mapping with the segment anything model
abstract: Accurate and transferable surface water mapping is critical for water resource assessment, flood monitoring, and aquatic ecosystem management, but remains difficult because SAR speckle, optical contamination, heterogeneous backgrounds, and scarce high-quality pixel-level annotations limit robust large-scale mapping. We propose SAMWater, a prompt-guided multimodal framework that integrates Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical imagery, the Segment Anything Model (SAM), and Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3). Instead of using SAR and optical data as independent classifiers, SAMWater transforms their complementary information into structured prompts for coarse-to-refined water segmentation. A physically interpretable multisensor coarse water prior is first generated from Sentinel observations using an automatic threshold-based strategy. This prior is then refined through prompt-based boundary refinement, a multi-prompt excavation strategy that derives point, box, and Gaussian-style mask prompts, and Water-IoU fine-tuning for water-specific candidate ranking. Using globally distributed samples and manually interpreted PlanetScope reference labels, SAMWater achieved average Kappa coefficients of 90.71%, 85.63%, and 89.05% in evaluations stratified by water body type, land cover background, and climatic zone, respectively. It generally outperformed traditional thresholding and clustering methods, public deep learning models, and existing global water or land cover products, particularly in structurally complex river, reservoir, urban, agricultural, and mountainous scenes. Ablation experiments confirmed that multimodal prior fusion, structured prompt construction, and water-specific ranking jointly drive the performance gains. Moreover, SAMWater-generated refined labels improved the training of U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer, indicating their utility for weakly supervised segmentation. SAMWater therefore demonstrates that integrating physically interpretable remote sensing priors with promptable foundation models provides a practical pathway for transferable surface water mapping, large-scale multisensor weak-label generation, and more consistent monitoring of surface water extent.

title: Tracking vegetation disturbance, recovery, and sustainability in open-pit mining areas of Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region from 2000 to 2024
abstract: Evaluating the overarching efficacy of mine greening initiatives and supporting land resource management within open-pit mining areas requires accurate long-term monitoring of both vegetative degradation and its subsequent regenerative phases. Overcoming the bottlenecks of conventional methods in decoupling vegetation abrupt disturbances from gradual recovery processes, this research utilizes the Google Earth Engine (GEE) and Landsat data spanning from 2000 to 2024. The investigation explicitly targets open-pit mining areas across the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region. Through the synergistic integration of the Continuous Change Detection and Classification (CCDC) and an adaptively refined NDVImed,t segmentation baseline, we extracted the spatiotemporal dynamics of abrupt vegetation disturbance and gradual recovery events. Furthermore, to rigorously quantify the enduring stability and long-term persistence of these vegetation dynamic trajectories, the study coupled the non-parametric Sen–MK trend estimator with calculations of the Hurst exponent. The results demonstrate that the F1 score for detecting disturbance and recovery events over the past 25 years stably exceeded 0.8, exhibiting excellent temporal robustness. The derived chronological trajectories pinpoint 2013 as a significant turning point for vegetation dynamics. Before this critical juncture, the landscape suffered from intense degradation, marked by an average annual vegetative deficit of 962.19 ha. In the post-2013 era, a recovery-dominated paradigm emerged, characterized by an average yearly restoration of 831.37 ha. Crucially, the aggregate intensity of this vegetation greenness reached 1.64, substantially overshadowing the historical extraction-induced disturbance magnitude of 1.23. Concurrently, evaluations of trajectory persistence reveal that while a substantial 36.56% of the monitored landscape is undergoing sustained ecological enhancement, whereas 22.46% was characterized by persistent deterioration. Precipitation and temperature showed a limited influence on vegetation dynamics (R2 = 0.0796, p = 0.402), while enterprise consolidation and reclamation policies were the main drivers for post-2013 recovery. The acquired quantitative remote sensing evidence not only reveals the core role of macro-policy regulation in driving the reshaping of surface landscapes in mining areas but also provides solid scientific support for the future refined ecological governance of regional territorial space.

title: A review of remote sensing for agricultural drought: technologies, indices, modelling advances and future prospects
abstract: Agricultural drought is a complex hazard that jeopardises food security and progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. We systematically reviewed peer-reviewed English-language literature published between 2015 and 2025, focusing on Remote Sensing (RS)-driven agricultural drought monitoring and prediction. Eligible studies were identified from the Web of Science and Scopus databases (last searched in August 2025); review articles, duplicates, and irrelevant studies were excluded, resulting in 181 articles. This review critically examined the evolution of sensors, drought indices, modelling approaches, and emerging technologies used to assess agricultural drought across diverse agro-ecological regions. Specifically, we (1) systematically evaluated the use of optical, thermal, and microwave RS platforms, along with satellite-based, model-based, and reanalysis products for agricultural drought monitoring; (2) reviewed widely used RS-based drought indices, including single indices grouped into nine categories, as well as composite indices; (3) reviewed software or programming languages applied; (4) assessed the progression of modelling approaches from traditional statistical and time-series methods to machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) frameworks; and (5) examined validation strategies applied to agricultural drought assessment. The analysis reveals a growing research interest in this topic, with a strong geographic concentration in Asia, particularly China. Optical and thermal platforms (e.g. MODIS and Landsat) dominate the literature (~54%) due to their accessibility, followed by satellite-derived precipitation products (17%), while microwave soil-moisture missions remain underutilized (~7%). Regarding RS-based indices, most studies employed more than one index: 44% analysed multiple individual indices, 51% used composite indices (either alone or in combination with individual indices), and only 5% relied on a single index. Vegetation indices, such as NDVI, remain workhorses; however, their sensitivity to soil background effects and canopy saturation has driven increased adoption of thermal composites (e.g. VHI), as well as adaptive weighting schemes and principal component analysis-based approaches. Moreover, computational tools used in drought research can be broadly grouped into geospatial and RS platforms for large-scale data processing and analysis (e.g. QGIS, GEE), and general-purpose programming languages (e.g. R, Python) for model development and advanced analytics. Regarding the methodology, statistical and time-series approaches account for 64% of the reviewed studies, followed by ML models (20%) and DL methods (15%), while explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) remains nascent. Techniques, such as random forests, support vector machines, and CNN and LSTM architectures, generally outperform traditional models but require large training datasets and raise concerns related to interpretability and ethics. In terms of validation, hydro-climatic indices such as SPI and SPEI are most commonly used (32%), followed by crop yield and yield anomaly data (19%). This review further identifies key research gaps across sensors, indices, and modelling approaches and proposes a roadmap for developing equitable, interpretable, and resilient agricultural drought monitoring systems. Emerging opportunities include context-aware and interpretable AI, multi-sensor and multi-scale data fusion across optical, thermal, and microwave domains, integration of physiologically meaningful indicators such as sun-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), robust uncertainty quantification, and the development of hybrid and physics-informed modelling frameworks.

title: Point-Cloud-Native L-Band Augmentation of SWOT KaRIn: Recovering Canopy-Shadowed Dark Water with NISAR
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: The SWOT mission's Ka-band Radar Interferometer (KaRIn) delivers surface-water observations at 15-25 m resolution but the operational Level-2 Pixel Cloud is known to miss pixels where dense canopy attenuates the specular return, flagging them as dark water. We show that co-registering NISAR L-band geocoded backscatter onto SWOT PIXC recovers dark-water pixels at matched precision. Over the Congo cuvette the augmentation lifts dark-water recall by 11.3 pp; over the Amazon varzea by 17.9 pp. Both gains clear a pre-registered 10 pp kill gate with disjoint 95% bootstrap confidence intervals versus baseline. A joint-shuffle falsifier confirms the gain is from real sensor information, not regularisation. To our knowledge this is the first combined use of NISAR and SWOT reported quantitatively.

title: Dual Retrieval Queries Fine-Tuning for Composed Image Retrieval
abstract: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) is a popular multi-modal retrieval task that aims to retrieve a target image based on a query composed of a reference image and modification text. The challenge lies in how to effectively retrieve a target image that preserves the visual content of the reference image while incorporating the changes described by the modification text. Existing CIR methods primarily employ a fusion-based strategy or a textual-inversion strategy during training. Although these methods have achieved promising results, they are limited in fully leveraging multi-modal information. This results in modality redundancy, where the retrieval process is dominated by one modality while ignoring the other. To address this issue, we propose an asymmetric fusion mechanism to generate dual retrieval queries of different granularity, enabling the model to fully use multi-modal information. Specifically, we propose a novel method termed Dual Retrieval Queries Fine-Tuning for Composed Image Retrieval (DRQ-CIR), which consists of two key components: 1) a Bilateral Multi-Modal Fusion (BMMF) module based on pre-trained VLMs, which combines the reference image and modification text to generate an enriched retrieval query; and 2) a Dual Retrieval Queries Fine-Tuning (DRQ-FT) module, which employs latent prompts to generate an enhanced retrieval query. Dual retrieval queries are used for contrastive learning with the target image to fine-tune the model and improve retrieval performance. Additionally, we introduce a bi-directional training paradigm to ensure retrieval consistency and further exploit the triplets. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our proposed method on four established benchmark datasets. (Code will be available at: https://github.com/Crystal-twy998/DRQ-CIR).

title: CycleDiff: Cycle Diffusion Models for Unpaired Image-to-image Translation
abstract: We introduce a diffusion-based cross-domain image translator in the absence of paired training data. Unlike GAN-based methods, our approach integrates diffusion models to learn the image translation process, allowing for more coverable modeling of the data distribution and performance improvement of the cross-domain translation. However, incorporating the translation process within the diffusion process is still challenging since the two processes are not aligned exactly, i.e., the diffusion process is applied to the noisy signal while the translation process is conducted on the clean signal. As a result, recent diffusion-based studies employ separate training or shallow integration to learn the two processes, yet this may cause the local minimal of the translation optimization, constraining the effectiveness of diffusion models. To address the problem, we propose a novel joint learning framework that aligns the diffusion and the translation process, thereby improving the global optimality. Specifically, we propose to extract the image components with diffusion models to represent the clean signal and employ the translation process with the image components, enabling an end-to- end joint learning manner. On the other hand, we introduce a time-dependent translation network to learn the complex translation mapping, resulting in effective translation learning and significant performance improvement. Benefiting from the design of joint learning, our method enables global optimization of both processes, enhancing the optimality and achieving improved fidelity and structural consistency. We have conducted extensive experiments on RGB↔RGB and diverse cross-modality translation tasks including RGB↔Edge, RGB↔Semantics and RGB↔Depth, showcasing better generative performances than the state of the arts. Especially, our method achieves the best FID score in widely-adopted tasks and outperforms the second-best method with an improved FID of 19.61 and 19.67 on Dog→Cat and Dog→Wild respectively.

title: HazyDet: Open-Source Benchmark for Drone-View Object Detection With Depth Cues in Hazy Scenes
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Object detection from aerial platforms under adverse atmospheric conditions, particularly haze, is paramount to robust drone autonomy. Yet, this domain remains largely underexplored, primarily hindered by the absence of specialized benchmarks. To bridge this gap, we presentHazyDet, the first, large-scale benchmark specifically designed for drone-view object detection in hazy conditions. Comprising 383,000 real-world instances derived from both naturally hazy captures and synthetically hazed scenes augmented from clear images, HazyDet provides a challenging and realistic testbed for advancing detection algorithms. To address the severe visual degradation induced by haze, we propose the Depth-Conditioned Detector (DeCoDet), a novel architecture that integrates a Depth-Conditioned Kernel to dynamically modulate feature representations based on depth cues. The practical efficacy and robustness of DeCoDet are further enhanced by its training with a Progressive Domain Fine-Tuning (PDFT) strategy to mitigate synthetic-to-real domain shifts, and a Scale-Invariant Refurbishment Loss (SIRLoss) to ensure resilient learning from potentially noisy depth annotations. Comprehensive empirical validation on HazyDet substantiates the superiority of our unified DeCoDet framework, which achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing the closest competitor by a notable +1.0% mAP on challenging real-world hazy test scenarios. Our dataset and toolkit are available at https://github.com/GrokCV/HazyDet.

title: Copy–Move Forgery Detection and Question-Answering for Remote Sensing Image
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Driven by practical demands in land resource monitoring and national defense security, this paper introduces the Remote Sensing Copy-Move Question Answering (RSCMQA) task. Unlike traditional Remote Sensing Visual Question Answering (RSVQA), RSCMQA focuses on interpreting complex tampering scenarios and inferring relationships between objects. We present a suite of global RSCMQA datasets, comprising images from 29 different regions across 14 countries. Specifically, we propose five distinct datasets, including the basic dataset RS-CMQA, the category-balanced dataset RS-CMQA-B, the high-authenticity dataset Real-RSCM, the extended dataset RS-TQA, and the extended category-balanced dataset RS-TQA-B. These datasets fill a critical gap in the field while ensuring comprehensiveness, balance, and challenging scenarios. Furthermore, we introduce a region-discrimination-guided multimodal copy-move forgery perception framework (CMFPF), which enhances the accuracy of answering questions about tampered images by leveraging prompts about the differences and connections between the source and tampered regions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method establishes a stronger benchmark for RSCMQA compared to general VQA and RSVQA models. Our datasets and code are publicly available at https://github.com/shenyedepisa/RSCMQA.

title: Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulation Testbed for Geomagnetic Navigation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Geomagnetic navigation leverages the ubiquitous Earth's magnetic signals to navigate missions, without dependence on GPS services or pre-stored geographic maps. It has drawn increasing attention and is promising particularly for long-range navigation into unexplored areas. Current geomagnetic navigation studies are still in the early stages with simulations and computational validations, without concrete efforts to develop cost-friendly test platforms that can empower deployment and experimental analysis of the developed approaches. This paper presents a hardware-in-the-loop simulation testbed to support geomagnetic navigation experimentation. Our testbed is dedicated to synthesizing geomagnetic field environment for the navigation. We develop the software in the testbed to simulate the dynamics of the navigation environment, and we build the hardware to generate the physical magnetic field, which follows and aligns with the simulated environment. The testbed aims to provide controllable magnetic field that can be used to experiment with geomagnetic navigation in labs, thus avoiding real and expensive navigation experiments, e.g., in the ocean, for validating navigation prototypes. We build the testbed with off-the-shelf hardware in an unshielded environment to reduce cost. We also develop the field generation control and hardware parameter optimization for quality magnetic field generation. We conduct a detailed performance analysis to show the quality of the field generation by the testbed, and we report the experimental results on performance indicators, including accuracy, uniformity, stability, and convergence of the generated field towards the target geomagnetic environment.

title: Adaptive Denoising Algorithm With Considering Terrestrial Slopes for Single-Photon LiDAR Point Cloud Data Processing
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: The development of new spaceborne single-photon LiDAR technology provides a new way to acquire high-accuracy three-dimensional (3D) information on the ground and ground targets. However, due to its high sensitivity to noise, the measurement data are highly susceptible to noise pollution, which largely reduces the accuracy and reliability of the original data. In this paper, a parallelogram denoising kernel (PDK) is proposed for extraction of signal photons from noises, which is closely in line with the characteristics of single photon point cloud data. During the denoising process, the PDK adaptively recognize signals by considering multiple terrestrial features such as slope, spatial density and noise rate. Especially when facing large terrestrial slopes and drastically terrestrial slope changes, the PDK is able to adapt to these situations by deforming the shape of PDK, thus improving the denoising accuracy. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through experimental analysis in four different types of terrains (flat, gentle slope, steep slope and cliff). The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can improve the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) by at least 50%, and the coefficient of determination (R2) by about 10% when compared to the conventional model.

title: SPECIAL: Zero-Shot Hyperspectral Image Classification With CLIP
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification aims to categorize each pixel in an HSI into a specific land cover class, which is crucial for applications such as remote sensing, environmental monitoring, and agriculture. Although deep learning-based HSI classification methods have achieved significant advancements, existing methods still rely on manually labeled data for training, which is both time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel zero-shot hyperspectral image classification framework based on CLIP (SPECIAL), aiming to eliminate the need for manual annotations. The SPECIAL framework consists of two main stages: (1) CLIP-based pseudo-label generation, and (2) noisy label learning. In the first stage, HSI is spectrally interpolated to produce RGB bands. These bands are subsequently classified using CLIP, resulting in noisy pseudo-labels that are accompanied by confidence scores. To improve the quality of these labels, we propose a scaling strategy that fuses predictions from multiple spatial scales. In the second stage, spectral information and a label refinement technique are incorporated to mitigate label noise and further enhance classification accuracy. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that our SPECIAL outperforms existing methods in zero-shot HSI classification, showing its potential for more practical applications. The code is available at https://github.com/LiPang/SPECIAL.

title: Discriminating Cloud Particle Types Using Ground-Based Scanning Lidar: Theoretical Model and Experimental Analysis
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Accurately identifying cloud particle types is essential for improving cloud microphysical parameterizations and remote sensing retrievals. In this study, we develop a novel discrimination method for cloud particles using scanning lidar observations near the zenith, based on the theoretical backscattering properties of ice crystals. We introduce, for the first time, the use of the coefficient of variation (CV) and the variation coefficient difference (ΔCV) to quantify the variability of lidar backscatter signals during scanning. By integrating these metrics with depolarization ratio at the zenith direction (δ0) and ambient temperature, cloud particles are classified into seven categories: liquid water, liquid/mixed-phase, 2D ice crystals (quasi-horizontally oriented), 3D ice crystals (randomly oriented), mixed 2D+3D ice crystals, aggregated ice crystals, and droxtal ice crystals. Meanwhile, based on theoretical analysis, we introduced the high depolarization coverage (HDC) metric to improve the accuracy of distinguishing mixed 2D+3D ice crystals from liquid water or ice-liquid mixtures. After more than six months of continuous observations, the feasibility of the new algorithm was demonstrated through comprehensive observational analyses. Additionally, we also observed vertical layering of different cloud particle types within some mixed-phase clouds. In these clouds, 2D ice crystals tend to occur in the upper regions, mixed 2D+3D ice crystals are more common in the middle layers, while 3D or aggregated ice crystals are typically found in the lower parts of the cloud. Our proposed observational strategy and discrimination algorithm hold promise for providing new insights into cloud microphysics, which will further contribute to future climate change studies.

title: RFI-Net: Enhancing Passive Sensing Through Deep Learning-Based Time–Frequency Domain Radio Frequency Interference Detection and Mitigation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Radio-frequency interference (RFI) poses a significant challenge to passive sensing, which relies on extremely sensitive measurements of natural thermal emissions. As radiometers increasingly operate in spectrally congested environments, often outside protected bands, accurate RFI detection becomes critical to ensure data integrity and enable spectrum coexistence. This paper presents RFI-Net, a deep learning-based framework for RFI detection and mitigation in the time-frequency (TF) domain. The model employs a U-Net architecture trained with a physicsinformed dual-loss strategy: a binary cross-entropy (BCE) loss targets detection of RFI-contaminated TF bins, while a mean squared error (MSE) loss minimizes deviations in estimated Brightness Temperature after RFI suppression at the same time. By removing corrupted bins and using only uncontaminated TF data, the framework enables reliable estimation of Brightness Temperature. RFI-Net is evaluated on a synthetic dataset simulating multiple interference scenarios with varying interference-tonoise ratios (INRs), spectral occupancy, duty cycles, and various communication and radar waveform types to capture both pulsed and continuous wave RFI characteristics. Additionally, real-world validation is performed using a spectrum coexistence testbed dataset, where an L-band radiometer is exposed to 5G signals with different power levels and resource block group allocations. Compared to the widely used spectral kurtosis method, RFI-Net achieves superior performance in detection metrics of accuracy, precision, recall, and as well as MSE of Brightness Temperature.

title: Monitoring Planted Forest Expansion From 1990 to 2020 in China
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: China has undertaken extensive afforestation efforts in recent decades. However, the effectiveness of these plantings varies with different environmental conditions. Whether China's forest expansion is primarily due to intentional planting or natural reforestation remains uncertain. Thus, assessing the growth of planted forests (PF) is crucial for monitoring forest quality and supporting China’s commitment to carbon neutrality. In this study, using 30 m Landsat time-series, we proposed a Continuous Change Detection and Classification (CCDC)-based PF expansion monitoring (C-PFM) method. Based on the C-PFM, 30 m annual maps for PF and natural forests (NF) across China from 1990 and 2020 were produced. The resulting PF map in 2020 achieved a F1-score of 79.2 % for PF and an overall accuracy of 90.8 % when validated against visually interpreted reference data. The PF maps for the years 1998, 2003, 2008, 2013, and 2018 were evaluated using data from the 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th National Forest Inventory (NFI) data across 34 provinces and autonomous regions of China. The results demonstrated that all Pearson’s product-moment correlations were larger than 0.86. According to the C-PFM results, we found 8.06 million ha (Mha) of net forest gains across China from 1990 to 2020, with 16.15 Mha net gains of PF and 8.09 Mha net loss of NF. In eight forestry ecological engineering areas, we observed that the upper and middle reaches of Yangtze river Shelterbelt Program and Pearl River Shelterbelt Program experienced the most significant PF expansion. The resulting dataset can serve as valuable scientific data for policymakers, researchers, and forest managers, guiding appropriate planting, environment enhancement, and carbon sequestration efforts. The produced 30 m annual maps for PF and NF in China are publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15559086 (Xiao, 2025).

title: RIVDCB-UNet: A Robust Vessel Detection in Cluttered Backgrounds via UNet for SDGSAT-1 Thermal-Infrared Data
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Aiming at complex and variable scenarios with cloud and fog obscuration and diverse interference sources, a robust infrared vessel detection in cluttered backgrounds via the UNet (RIVDCB-UNet) is designed. This model effectively overcomes the limitations of traditional UNet in small target detection and significantly improves its detection performance. The RIVDCB-UNet model takes a single thermal infrared image as input and incorporates the BCE-Dice loss function to ensure stability and accuracy during the training process. The model integrates the EfficientNet backbone network for efficient feature extraction, followed by feature upsampling and fusion through a U-shaped decoder. Finally, an eight-connected neighborhood clustering module is introduced to further refine pixel-level classification results and achieve precise localization. The training of the proposed model leverages the publicly available NUDT-SIRST-Sea Dataset and our self-constructed SDGSAT-1 thermal infrared vessel detection dataset. Data augmentation techniques, including rotation and cropping, are employed to expand the dataset, thereby addressing the issue of target-background imbalance in the original datasets. This imbalance can cause the model to overly focus on information-sparse background regions. The proposed model achieves detection rates, recall rates, and F1 scores of 95.39%, 97.89%, 96.62% on the NUDT-SIRST-Sea Dataset, and 97.81%, 96.78%, 97.29% on the SDGSAT-1 dataset, respectively. These results are significantly higher than those of other models such as ACM (84.81%, 73.17%, 78.56% on NUDT-SIRST-Sea and 90.17%, 72.87%, 80.60% on SDGSAT-1) and DNANet (89.98%, 83.10%, 86.40% on NUDT-SIRST-Sea and 95.64%, 88.21%, 91.77% on SDGSAT-1).

title: Sensing Accuracy Optimization for Multi-UAV SAR Interferometry with Data Offloading
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: The integration of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) with radar imaging sensors has revolutionized the monitoring of dynamic and local Earth surface processes by enabling high-resolution and cost-effective remote sensing. This paper investigates the optimization of the sensing accuracy of a UAV swarm deployed to perform multi-baseline interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) sensing. In conventional single-baseline InSAR systems, only one synthetic aperture radar (SAR) antenna pair acquires two SAR images from two distinct angles to generate a digital elevation model (DEM) of the target area. However, multi-baseline InSAR extends this concept by aggregating multiple acquisitions from different angles, thus, significantly enhancing the vertical accuracy of the DEM. The heavy computations required for this process are performed on the ground and, therefore, the radar data is transmitted in real time to a ground station (GS) via a frequency-division multiple access (FDMA) air-to-ground backhaul link. This work focuses on improving the sensing precision by minimizing the height error of the averaged DEM while simultaneously ensuring sensing and communication quality-of-service (QoS). To this end, the UAV formation, velocity, and communication power allocation are jointly optimized using evolutionary algorithms (EAs). Our approach is benchmarked against established optimization methods, including genetic algorithms (GAs), simulated annealing (SA), and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) techniques. Numerical results show that the proposed solution outperforms these baseline schemes and achieves sub-decimeter vertical accuracy in several scenarios. These findings underline the potential of coordinated UAV swarms for delivering high-precision and real-time Earth observations through radar interferometry.

title: Compact Multilevel-Prior Tensor Representation for Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Fusing a hyperspectral image with a multispectral image acquired over the same scene, \textit{i.e.}, hyperspectral image super-resolution, has become a popular computational way to access the latent high-spatial-spectral-resolution image. To date, a variety of fusion methods have been proposed, among which the tensor-based ones have testified that multiple priors, such as multidimensional low-rankness and spatial total variation at multiple levels, effectively drive the fusion process. However, existing tensor-based models can only effectively leverage one or two priors at one or two levels, since simultaneously incorporating multi-level priors inevitably increases model complexity. This introduces challenges in both balancing the weights of different priors and optimizing multi-block structures. Concerning this, we present a novel hyperspectral super-resolution model compactly characterizing these multi-level priors of hyperspectral images within the tensor framework. Firstly, the proposed model decouples the spectral low-rankness and spatial priors by casting the latent high-spatial-spectral-resolution image into spectral subspace and spatial maps via block term decomposition. Secondly, these spatial maps are stacked as the spatial tensor encoding the high-order spatial low-rankness and smoothness priors, which are co-modeled via the proposed non-convex mode-shuffled tensor correlated total variation. Finally, we draw inspiration from the linearized alternating direction method of multipliers to design an efficient algorithm to optimize the resulting model, theoretically proving its Karush-Kuhn-Tucker convergence under mild conditions. Experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. The code implementation will be available from https://github.com/WongYinJ.

title: Seismic Acoustic Impedance Inversion Framework Based on Conditional Latent Generative Diffusion Model
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Seismic acoustic impedance plays a crucial role in lithological identification and subsurface structure interpretation. However, due to the inherently ill-posed nature of the inversion problem, directly estimating impedance from post-stack seismic data remains highly challenging. Recently, diffusion models have shown great potential in addressing such inverse problems due to their strong prior learning and generative capabilities. Nevertheless, most existing methods operate in the pixel domain and require multiple iterations, limiting their applicability to field data. To alleviate these limitations, we propose a novel seismic acoustic impedance inversion framework based on a conditional latent generative diffusion model, where the inversion process is made in latent space. To avoid introducing additional training overhead when embedding conditional inputs, we design a lightweight wavelet-based module into the framework to project seismic data and reuse an encoder trained on impedance to embed low-frequency impedance into the latent space. Furthermore, we propose a model-driven sampling strategy during the inversion process of this framework to enhance accuracy and reduce the number of required diffusion steps. Numerical experiments on a synthetic model demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high inversion accuracy and strong generalization capability within only a few diffusion steps. Moreover, application to field data reveals enhanced geological detail and higher consistency with well-log measurements, validating the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed approach.

title: MSGFusion: Multimodal Scene Graph-Guided Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Infrared and visible image fusion aims to generate high-quality images with both rich low-level details and clear high-level semantics. Yet, prevailing data-driven approaches remain largely confined to interactions at the level of low-level features, such as pixel intensities or gradients. Although some task-driven methods introduce semantic constraints via downstream labels, such as object detection or semantic segmentation, they are limited to implicit priors or local regions, struggling to provide global, context-aware structured semantic guidance. Recent text-driven methods attempt to incorporate unstructured textual priors; however, directly injecting them into low-level fusion networks often disrupts the inherent spatial and semantic coherence, ultimately leading to edge distortion and texture degradation. We therefore present MSGFusion, a novel multimodal scene graph-guided image fusion framework designed to bridge the representation gap between high-level semantics and the low-level pixel space. By deeply coupling structured scene graphs derived from both text and vision, MSGFusion explicitly represents entities, attributes, and spatial relations. It subsequently aligns the parsed structured semantics to specific local visual regions through successive modules for scene graph representation, hierarchical aggregation, and scene graph-driven fusion. This framework reformulates traditional pixel-level aggregation into spatially associated and semantically aware fine-grained fusion. Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmarks confirm that MSGFusion significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, yielding prominent advantages in detail preservation and structural clarity. Furthermore, the proposed method not only exhibits outstanpding semantic consistency in downstream tasks like pedestrian detection and semantic segmentation, but also features high computational efficiency and strong cross-domain generalization capabilities in medical image fusion tasks.Code is available at: https://github.com/KazDong628/MSGFusion.

title: 10k Is Enough: An Ultralightweight-Binarized Network for Infrared Small-Target Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: The widespread deployment of Infrared Small-Target Detection (IRSTD) algorithms on edge devices necessitates the exploration of model compression techniques. Binarized neural networks (BNNs) are distinguished by their exceptional efficiency in model compression. However, the small size of infrared targets introduces stringent precision requirements for the IRSTD task, while the inherent precision loss during binarization presents a significant challenge. To address this, we propose a Binarized Infrared Small-Target Detection Network (BiisNet), which preserves the core operations of binarized convolutions while integrating full-precision features into the network’s information flow. Specifically, we propose a Dot Binary Convolution to retain fine-grained semantic information in feature maps while still leveraging the binarized convolution operations. In addition, we introduce a smooth and adaptive Dynamic Softsign function, which provides more comprehensive and progressively finer gradient during backpropagation, enhancing model stability and promoting an optimal weight distribution. Experimental results demonstrate that BiisNet achieves anmIoUof 68.23% with only 10k parameters, delivering an 11.56% improvement over the previous best binary neural network while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art full-precision models. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/joeyxin-del/BiisNet.

title: BLMRS: A Balanced Learning Method for Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Multimodal remote sensing image classification provides essential support for fine-grained understanding of the Earth’s surface by fusing complementary information. Yet, multimodal fusion often suffers from a modal imbalance problem, where applying a uniform optimization objective leads to the under-optimization of certain modalities, posing a bottleneck to realizing the full benefits of fusion. Existing balanced learning strategies attempt to solve this problem by emphasizing the training of encoders for weaker modalities. However, in remote sensing scenarios, they overlook the domain-specific reality that certain weaker modalities inherently lack discriminative information; for example, the LiDAR-derived Digital Surface Model (DSM), which does not provide the necessary detail to effectively distinguish between land cover types. Indiscriminately emphasizing the learning of such modalities may introduce noise and impair the model’s overall performance. To address this, this work proposes a Balanced Learning Method for Multimodal Remote Sensing image classification (BLMRS). The method takes unimodal training in a non-competitive environment as a reference, and uses its output as the guidance signals to dynamically adjust the optimization preference in multimodal learning. This allows adaptive optimization for weaker modalities, avoiding overemphasis when their discriminative information is limited. To further avoid conflicts among guidance signals from different unimodal sources, we measure and filter out components inconsistent with the weaker modality’s guidance, ensuring the training focus remains on it. BLMRS is architecture-agnostic and can be seamlessly integrated into existing classification backbones. Extensive experiments on four public benchmarks and six backbone architectures demonstrate that our method consistently offers performance gains. It remains robust even when a modality’s discriminative information is degraded.

title: Multilayer Ionosphere Correction in Low-Frequency Interferometric SAR: Modeling, Inversion, and Application to BIOMASS
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Early analysis of BIOMASS interferometric data acquired during the commissioning phase at Boreal and Antarctic latitudes revealed the presence of strong ionospheric disturbances that cause severe coherence losses. This phenomenon was investigated by studying the variation of the interferometric phase with respect to the squint angle. Results are consistent with the assumption of a complex vertical structure of the ionospheric phase, characterized by fast azimuth variations occurring at Km or sub-Km scale at multiple layers between the ground and the satellite orbit. To the best of our knowledge this phenomenon has never been considered in Synthetic Aperture Radar literature. This paper is therefore intended to present and discuss the results of our investigation on suitable correction methods needed to guarantee the generation of accurate geophysical products from BIOMASS interferometric data. The starting point of our analysis is a multi-layered model of the ionospheric phase as observed by varying the Radar Line of Sight (LoS) across different squint angles. The model is analyzed from a theoretical perspective to discuss the sensitivity of BIOMASS to ionospheric layering. Next, an inversion procedure is presented to estimate the ionospheric phase at an arbitrary number of layers directly from the complex coherence. The third element of our research consists in the formulation of correction methods to restore data quality given the estimated single-or multi-layer ionospheric phase. All aspects of the research are consistently supported by analysis of BIOMASS interferometric data acquired at different latitudes and affected by mild to very strong ionospheric disturbances. Results demonstrate that the methodologies presented in this paper are capable of compensating for the observed ionospheric effects in all cases analyzed so far.

title: DFYP: A Dynamic Fusion Framework With Spectral Channel Attention and Adaptive Operator Learning for Crop Yield Prediction
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Accurate remote sensing-based crop yield prediction remains a fundamental challenging task due to complex spatial patterns, heterogeneous spectral characteristics, and dynamic agricultural conditions. Existing methods often suffer from limited spatial modeling capacity, weak generalization across crop types and years. To address these challenges, we propose DFYP, a novel Dynamic Fusion framework for crop Yield Prediction, which combines spectral channel attention, edge-adaptive spatial modeling and a learnable fusion mechanism to improve robustness across diverse agricultural scenarios. Specifically, DFYP introduces three key components: (1) aResolution-aware Channel Attention (RCA)module that enhances spectral representation by adaptively reweighting input channels based on resolution-specific characteristics; (2) anAdaptive Operator Learning Network (AOL-Net)that dynamically selects operators for convolutional kernels to improve edge-sensitive spatial feature extraction under varying crop and temporal conditions; and (3) adual-branch architecturewith a learnable fusion mechanism, which jointly models local spatial details and global contextual information to support cross-resolution and cross-crop generalization. Extensive experiments on multi-year datasets MODIS and multi-crop dataset Sentinel-2 demonstrate that DFYP consistently outperforms current state-of-the-art baselines in RMSE, MAE, and R² across different spatial resolutions, crop types, and time periods, showcasing its effectiveness and robustness for real-world agricultural monitoring.

title: KunPeng: A Global Ocean Environmental Model
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Inspired by the similarity of the atmosphere-ocean physical coupling mechanism, this study innovatively migrates meteorological large-model techniques to the ocean domain, constructing the KunPeng global ocean environmental prediction model. Aimed at the discontinuous characteristics of marine space, we propose a terrain-adaptive mask constraint mechanism to mitigate effectively training divergence caused by abrupt gradients at land-sea boundaries. To fully integrate far-, medium-, and close-range marine features, a longitude-cyclic deformable convolution network (LC-DCN) is employed to enhance the dynamic receptive field, achieving refined modeling of multi-scale oceanic characteristics. A Deformable Convolution-enhanced Multi-Step Prediction module (DC-MTP) is employed to strengthen temporal dependency feature extraction capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that this model achieves an average ACC of 0.80 in 15-day global predictions at 0.25$^\circ$ resolution, outperforming comparative models by 0.01-0.08. The average mean squared error (MSE) is 0.41 (representing a 5%-31% reduction) and the average mean absolute error (MAE) is 0.44 (0.6%-21% reduction) compared to other models. Significant improvements are particularly observed in sea surface parameter prediction, deep-sea region characterization, and current velocity field forecasting. Through a horizontal comparison of the applicability of operators at different scales in the marine domain, this study reveals that local operators significantly outperform global operators under slow-varying oceanic processes, demonstrating the effectiveness of dynamic feature pyramid representations in predicting marine physical parameters.

title: Semantics-Aware Hierarchical Consensus Learning for Remote Sensing Image Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Deep learning has become increasingly important in remote sensing image classification due to its ability to extract semantic information from complex data. Classification tasks often include predefined label hierarchies that represent the semantic relationships among classes. However, these hierarchies are frequently overlooked, and most approaches focus only on fine-grained classification schemes. In this paper, we present a novel Semantics-Aware Hierarchical Consensus (SAHC) approach that integrates hierarchical-level-specific classification heads within a deep network architecture and combines their output through cross-level probability projectors. Direct and projected predictions are fused into a geometric consensus distribution, which is used for self-consistent training and optional hierarchy-aware inference. This mechanism acts as a geometric ensemble that leverages the inherent structure of the hierarchical classification task. The projectors are initialized from the user-defined taxonomy (i.e., the hierarchical label structure), and can be adaptively refined during optimization. The proposed SAHC method is evaluated on two benchmark datasets with different degrees of hierarchical complexity on different tasks, considering varying spectral and spatial resolutions. Experimental results show both the effectiveness of the proposed approach in guiding network learning and the robustness of the hierarchical consensus for remote sensing image classification tasks. The source code is available at https://github.com/rslab-unitrento/sahc.

title: Adaptive Gradient Calibration for Single-Positive Multi-Label Learning in Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Multi-label classification (MLC) offers a more comprehensive semantic understanding of Remote Sensing (RS) imagery compared to traditional single-label classification (SLC). However, obtaining complete annotations for MLC is particularly challenging due to the complexity and high cost of the labeling process. As a practical alternative, single-positive multi-label learning (SPML) has emerged, where each image is annotated with only one relevant label, and the model is expected to recover the full set of labels. While scalable, SPML introduces significant supervision ambiguity, demanding specialized solutions for model training. Although various SPML methods have been proposed in the computer vision domain, research in the RS context remains limited. To bridge this gap, we propose Adaptive Gradient Calibration (AdaGC), a novel and generalizable SPML framework tailored to RS imagery. AdaGC adopts a gradient calibration (GC) mechanism with a dual exponential moving average (EMA) module for robust pseudo-label generation. We introduce a theoretically grounded, training-dynamics-based indicator to adaptively trigger GC, which ensures GC’s effectiveness by preventing it from being affected by model underfitting or overfitting to label noise. Extensive experiments on two benchmark RS datasets under two distinct label noise types demonstrate that AdaGC achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance while maintaining strong robustness across diverse settings. The codes and data will be released at https://github.com/rslab-unitrento/AdaGC.

title: DREMnet: An Interpretable Denoising Framework for Semi-Airborne Transient Electromagnetic Signal
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: The semi-airborne transient electromagnetic method (SATEM) is capable of conducting rapid surveys over large-scale and hard-to-reach areas. However, the acquired signals are often contaminated by complex noise, which can compromise the accuracy of subsequent inversion interpretations. Traditional denoising techniques primarily rely on parameter selection strategies, which are insufficient for processing field data in noisy environments. With the advent of deep learning, various neural networks have been employed for SATEM signal denoising. However, existing deep learning methods typically use single-mapping learning approaches that struggle to effectively separate signal from noise. These methods capture only partial information and lack interpretability. To overcome these limitations, we propose an interpretable decoupled representation learning framework, termed DREMnet, that disentangles data into content and context factors, enabling robust and interpretable denoising in complex conditions. To address the limitations of convolutional neural network (CNN) and transformer architectures, we utilize the receptance weighted key value (RWKV) architecture for data processing and introduce the contextual weighted key value (Co-WKV) mechanism, which allows unidirectional weighted key value (WKV) to perform bidirectional signal modeling. Our proposed Cover Embedding technique retains the strong local perception of convolutional networks through stacked embedding.
